text:
Mina (design): quick sync on rollout controls UI - trying a micro-accordion pattern for allocation chips instead of inline inputs. feels cleaner on narrow layouts. thoughts?
Ken: micro-accordion sounds promising. does it keep the percent visible at a glance? that's important for PMs doing quick checks.
Priya: we could show a compact chip like "Ramp 10%" and an affordance to expand to slider + exact field. preserves glanceability.
Diego: agree. bonus: when collapsed, chips are only buttons so we avoid accidental edits. but need an obvious affordance that it's expandable. an arrow + aria label maybe.
Mina (design): yes arrow + accessible name. copy-wise I'm leaning from "Canary" -> "Ramp" (shorter) with tooltip: "Staged rollout / canary / A-B". any objections?
Ken: +1 for "Ramp". shorter and less jargony. include a help link to docs for advanced targets.
Priya: accessibility nit: ensure the expanded panel is in DOM order after the chip so screen readers see allocation controls where focus lands. also add aria-live for the allocation summary so a change is announced.
Diego: implementation note: use aria-expanded on the chip button and move focus into the first control in the panel. on close return focus to the chip.
Mina (design): good. UX question: should the slider update live or require explicit "Apply"? I'm leaning explicit apply to avoid accidental traffic shifts.
Ken: explicit apply + lightweight toast confirmation with undo for 10s. also record reason in audit log for >= 20% changes.
Priya: reason field is good for audit. for small edits we can allow skip, but make it required for major ramps. set threshold in ops config.
Diego: also make the toast accessible: include a dismiss button, role=alert with polite live region, and keyboard focusable undo.
Mina (design): rollback flow: adding a quick rollback icon on hover of version dot is useful, but keyboard users need parity. propose a contextual action menu (kebab) on focus with "Rollback to this snapshot".
Ken: when rollback happens, prompt modal should avoid scary copy. Proposed copy: "Revert traffic to this snapshot. This changes live traffic but does not delete historical data. Please add an optional note for the audit log."
Priya: yes softer. and ensure modal focuses the note textarea first, trap focus, and return to timeline after close. also include a two-step confirm only when traffic delta > 30%.
Diego: perf note: timeline hover currently fires metrics fetch per hover. let's debounce 250ms and keep a tiny in-memory cache per page session. show cached sparkline immediately and fetch full metrics on expand.
Mina (design): sounds good. small visual: on hover/focus, add a faint dashed ring around version dot and show the action icon. make sure contrast meets AA for the ring.
Ken: CSS snippet for focus ring I'll use: ```css .version-dot:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(13,110,253,0.14); outline: none; } .alloc-chip { background: #fff; color: #021124; } ```
Priya: color contrast check: test the chip badge at small sizes. add an icon-only focus indicator for tight layouts.
ops-bot: preview deployed for branch "ux/ramp-micro-accordion" -> https://console.redwood.ai/preview/ux/ramp-accordion :white_check_mark:
Mina (design): thanks ops-bot. i'll upload updated frames to Figma (collapsed chip, expanded panel, rollback modal copy).
Diego: i'll add aria attributes, debounce, and cache in the timeline component. will also add unit tests for focus transfer.
Ken: i'll update copy in content repo and add tooltip text.
Priya: i'll run an a11y sweep on the mockups after Diego's changes. if all good, we aim to ship in the next iteration. :shipit:
Mina (design): perfect. follow-ups: Diego implements, Ken pushes copy PR, Priya validates a11y. ping here if blockers.
